title: The narrowest parameter
summary: Take the least you need: &str over &String, &[T] over &Vec<T>, borrow over own.
lecture: A signature is a contract about what the function may do with the data. Taking String says 'I consume this'; &mut String says 'I change it'; &str says 'I only look'. Callers can hand a narrower function more kinds of input with less ceremony - so the narrowest honest type is the kindest API.

Concretely: &String and &Vec<T> parameters are strictly worse than &str and &[T] - deref coercion means every caller of the slice version still works, plus literals, arrays, and sub-slices. Clippy's ptr_arg lint flags the former on sight.

This is also why 'it compiles' is a weak bar for API puzzles: several signatures compile, but they impose different costs on every future caller. The optimal one moves the fewest obligations across the boundary.

example.code:
fn join_tags(tags: &Vec<String>) -> String  // works, but rigid
fn join_tags(tags: &[String]) -> String     // same body, more callers
example.caption: The slice version accepts vecs, arrays, and sub-slices alike.
